After removal
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/192674c303192bcd04e8b3032d2cfb280fea4471.png
The cost of gear repair has already been adjusted and will not change after Repair Parts are removed.
Assault on the Reichstag
On May 8, 1945, the final Act of Unconditional Surrender of Nazi Germany and its armed forces was signed in the Berlin suburb of Karlshorst at 22 hours 43 minutes CET (May 9 at 0:43 Moscow time).
To honor this event, a time-limited session mode returns, which gradually becomes a tradition in our game!
From May 7 to 11, the Assault on the Reichstag map will be available in the “Session modes” menu.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/49c172b6338e50f73fe26964d43a2f30211de0b7.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/9fcb51c38b3416a780f426b9ab3fe3e722eb0694.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/8dfae99bf466237688c6f82866bef5746e4d8492.jpg
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/5c1c628b0d13c630ddf172597d634b7a079cf044.jpg
During this time, the Assault on the Reichstag will temporarily replace the DeathMatch mode and switch every hour with Arms Race. On May 9, the mode will be available all day long.
Mode features
• Players are given random themed equipment based on their team.
• Artillery strikes will periodically occur on the map.
• More powerful weapons can be found during combat.
• Kills and deaths on this map do not count toward a player’s overall statistics.
• Spartak’s inventory has been updated with the following themed gear: the PPSh and its modules, the Mauser 98k and its module, the Russian Bayonet, the Red Star Charm, and themed paints.
Balance changes
Stopping power
The passive removal rate of the stopping power has been increased from 20% to 80% per second.
Previously, when the stopping power fully wore off in 1.25 seconds, players could experience a sudden speed spike, causing an unpleasant “dash”. Now, movement speed will recover more smoothly and quickly.

Sights are exchanged at level 7 of the northern faction base. The exchange is available for 3 blueprint parts obtained from the northern faction crates and the weapon crate.

historical_patches.title: Patchnote [04.06.2025]
historical_patches.text:
The skies of the Zone are torn apart by the roar of military helicopters. Armed forces are gathering at the Perimeter. The ZIVCAS Corporation is once again searching for mysterious testing grounds left behind by scientists of the past. Behind the North anomaly barrier lies a power capable of pulverizing anyone who dares to uncover its secrets. Something is happening in the Zone. And it will affect everyone — whether they like it or not.
© A mad old man in the Bar that nobody's believed since the “hot July”
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/a20958dee34dea51779c301d243786d4ee290455.png
We bid farewell not only to the spring season but also to Act One — it was a special one for us, we'll never forget it. Act Tickets were converted into Trade coins. In memory of past seasons, all players who earned caskets have received them by mail — they are now usable as Hideout decor.
Today marks the beginning of a new stage — Act Two. And it brings not just new rewards, but a full change of rules: the Season Pass has undergone a complete overhaul, and with it, much of what players had grown used to.
Are you ready for a hot June? 🔥
Something strange is happening in the Zone
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/a3867c46f781bb77c1ac88932eb263ce7abef599.jpg
Things are getting tense. Military forces have been unusually active near the Perimeter in the South. We recommend staying alert, so you don’t miss any important information.
Season Pass: Reboot
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/93fd8aaf6e5e8281c6f0162d295bb86c70837de9.png
Season Pass was originally intended as a light, optional background activity, that accompanied the main gameplay, eventually turned into the main focus of the game, overshadowing other content.
We’ve addressed long-standing issues from previous seasons and made substantial changes to the Season Pass mechanics. In general terms, the following has changed:
• Removed Sealed Points, as they were the root of many problems.
• Progression is once again tied to daily tasks, now more engaging and customizable. Players can choose tasks categories to fit their play style.
• Valuable rewards have been greatly increased, making the Season Pass much more worthwhile.
Full breakdown of the changes available in a separate article.
Starting this season, all players who have completed the North storyline will automatically receive 50 Season Pass levels.
Open world changes
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/893d34515005fa3bbdb866709aac254ddbae3158.jpg
To diversify gameplay and space for Season Pass daily quests, we added new events with mutants and NPCs. Now you'll have fiends, snipers, sappers, and behemoths waiting for you in the North.
In addition, the old Anomalous Installations have been reworked, and new ones have been added. Now, when you activate them, instead of the usual spirits, you will be met with more worthy opponents.
Most of the new activity is concentrated in the home territories of the northern factions — now there’s actually something to do there.
Location events that are required to complete tasks will be highlighted when the map is opened.
Season rewards
500 level reward
The main reward of this season is the versatile Beretta ARX160 assault rifle with an underbarrel grenade launcher.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/2b9b2b9af0468041e6500395f4a990ada4297d53.jpg
This weapon is available for test firing in your Hideout — it sits right on the shooting range counter!
Updated Season Pass rewards
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/51da768006df8b594552178d9b8137a6059f39c4.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/3b48230d4c89991cb2d022192451be629f0bc6a9.jpg
Season crate
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/5f060feb08ccddadf97f38ccf6bac927d0685cd7.png
The season crate, named Gift of Murmur this season, has been overhauled along with the rest Season Pass content: all junk has been removed, the amount of valuable consumables was increased, and key rewards now drop much more frequently.
Gift of Murmur includes the following key rewards:
• JD ZIVCAS 2A Exoarmor parts;

New gear for Act tickets
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/61a1e4dfaeb453270c6503103fc430dc4db90d3d.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/137cb2229d76f667d48e8235e39cdf0101fb1484.png

The required number of parts and the price remain unchanged, you need to collect 8 parts, each of which costs 1000 Tickets.
New gear is available for Act II Tickets:

Murmur of the Zone styles
New styles themed to Murmur faction are available in the shop — a sinister fusion of steel and unknown materials born in the depths of the Zone.
The following items are available in the shop:
• Roar style for PKP Pecheneg;
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/c37a91944c7cb6c1653e02536fb3ec278f17a3af.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/8d9005276b31d7395358e175e45a4b76a95cf3ad.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/5d7741daedbab219687639b2bc362720d9f777de.png
• Swish style for Tactical katana (transferable version will be released later).
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/73f515b44ec1226184f2b7cca4d0ee65697f492c.png
These styles can be purchased personally or as gifts for friends or the auction trading.
Murmur of the Zone Starter Pack 
The Murmur of the Zone season starter pack is now available for purchase in the in-game store.
It includes the following items:
• 10 season levels;
• 7 day Premium;
• Two unique armour and weapon paints.
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/b6d95e4b29d0753fe18c6dcda7b82c3405787853.png
New Special case
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/b50deb16ff306db0079185c94b8e27aeaa46ce2d.jpg
Alongside the Season Pass, we’ve completely overhauled the transferable gear cases. The old gear cases have been merged into one ultimate Special Case!
You’ll be presented with three cards, each hiding a reward. After picking one, you'll see what was behind the other two — then they disappear. You can instantly claim your reward, sell it to other players for profit, or, if it’s not to your liking, reject it and get back part of the currency you spent.
Special case includes various items grouped by their rarity. Each case guarantees a standard rarity item. In addition, there’s a chance to obtain up to four bonus items of higher rarities. Ideally, you could get up to five items in total: one standard and four bonus ones — unique, rare, very rare, extremely rare.
Don’t worry if you don’t get bonus items right away: your chances of receiving one increase with each subsequent case you open, until a bonus item drops. Once that happens, the drop rate for that rarity tier resets to its base value — just like the first time you opened a case.
Special case key rewards:

• Albatross Interceptor;
• Elbrus SRD;

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/bf224e76eba4a9f5eacd90052816fc107d99d3ae.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/53a1abe8ed0e54f9b578d10f4f7b2496b51fb4d2.jpg
Transferable Season Pass levels
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/b904a76c90300a8a4a487a7219ab6af36331ce0b.png
Transferable Season Pass levels have been added to the in-game shop. You can now purchase them as a gift for another player or sell them via the auction.
There are 3 available bundles:
• 1 level — 109 SC;
• 10 levels — 1039 SC;
• 25 levels — 2299 SC.
Gear repair
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/0ee86aea0e5d84660798a7a007d8d255da39657e.jpg
Repair Parts have been removed from the game.
All old, sealed Parts will be compensated at a standard rate. Additionally, all players who had them will receive a small but memorable collectible item via in-game mail.
After analysing the gathered data and your feedback over the past month, we’ve decided to reduce repair costs by 20%. We understand that, even with this adjustment, the removal of Parts will still result in higher repair costs. However, this step is necessary to introduce another currency withdrawal method to help stabilize the in-game economy.
We will continue to monitor repair costs closely and appreciate your understanding.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41581512/05b5c66393a03a684b98f349d45d4785231b16d6.png

This change is aimed at increasing the difficulty of extracting highly valuable items, such as artefacts, and giving more weight to surviving during runs to obtain them.

historical_patches.title: Patchnote [07.06.2025]
historical_patches.text:
Hey!
Here are the very developers of Season Pass, still trapped in the basement and dreaming of food.
We didn't waste time: we implemented important changes to the mechanics within a couple of days to fix the bugs that came out on release.
Our particular thanks to those who gave us clear, constructive feedback — it helped us to quickly focus and make the right decisions.
Now, let's move on! What's new:
Changes in Season Pass points gain
We heard that many people miss weekly tasks, so we decided to remove the rewards for closing categories by adding points for weekly activities.
This will help players who can't play every day not be as far behind those who play daily.
• 
For 15 tasks — 3000 points;
• 
For 45 tasks — 5000 points;
• 
For 100 tasks — 12000 points.
Furthermore:
• 
Reward is now given for any daily tasks. It will be the same whether you are doing the task for the first time or repeatedly;
• 
Removed the gradual increase in difficulty of tasks after they are completed;
• 
The outline around icons for Season Pass activities has been fixed to improve clarity;
• 
Premium reward has been redesigned. It now grants extra vouchers for completing the weekly progress bar;
• 
Exploration bonus has been moved to make it easier and clearer to display. It was also done since not all players liked getting the reward in every quest: too many clicks and interactions with the interface. Now all the rewards accumulate in one place, and by clicking once, you can pick it all up whenever you want;
Apart from the interface, the exploration bonus has been adjusted as follows:
• 
First 7 tasks — 500 points;
• 
Following 8 tasks — 250 points each;
• 
Following 30 tasks — 75 points each;
• 
All the rest — 25 points each.
Task changes
Fixed bugs with counting the completion of some activities:
• 
Events located in the South of the Zone are now counted in the Clearing-out enemy outposts task;
• 
Fights on GOST-17 are now counted in the Completion of battles task of the Sessional Battles category;
• 
Damage to structures is now not counted in the Dealing damage to opponents task of the Subdivision Battles category;
• 
The Anomalous Rift event now counts as a weekly task.
Changed the content of task categories;
Changed the content of the open world events.
We've also added information about which locations you can find quests at to make it easier and more convenient to navigate.
Compensations
Players who did not complete the full weekly bonus for closing categories will be compensated. Their progress will be transferred to the new weekly task system.
Compensation for each closed category not rewarded will be equal to three weekly tasks completed.
The compensation will be displayed in the weekly bonus section, indicating how many tasks are already considered completed.
Changing the Overdrive mechanics
Overdrive gives a bonus for the first 15 completed tasks in a day, even if they are repetitive. In other words, it can be activated again after every 15 completions, even if it's the same task.
Overdrive bonus can be earned any time of the day, not only at the time of completing a task. If Overdrive is already activated, the bonus will still be received automatically;
Now for convenience and understanding, the specific number of season points that Overdrive gives is listed, specifically 250 points.
Other changes and fixes
• 
The Chicken God artefact now correctly gives a separate buff for each reaction, rather than upgrading the same one;
• 
Fixed failure to be able to select categories;
• 
Fixed the sights on the QBZ-191 “Burevestnik” and FN F2000 Tactical;
• 
Reduced the selling price of some items obtained from opening the Special Case;
• 
Reduced the volume of loudspeakers in safe zones.
Conclusion
That's all for now on the current changes. But don't even think that this is where we're going to end up! No. We won't be allowed to leave the basement for a long time: there's a lot of work ahead to finalise current tasks and add new ones, as well as to replace those that frankly didn't work. We'll be rotating the numbers in the dailies in parallel to equalise them in value.
It's a separate motivation to keep working with the open world. Like finally getting to the Labyrinth and finally touch it. We are ready to fight.
We will also continue to listen to feedback. We have already fixed, for example, poorly readable blackout of repetitive tasks. We also keep such little things in mind and will correct them as we go along. We'll keep it that way.
Anyway, we're not relaxing. Because there's something in the basement with us. And we better not piss it off.

historical_patches.title: Patchnote [11.06.2025]
historical_patches.text:
The sound of helicopter blades is getting louder in the airspace, and the ground is crawling with more patrols than ever.
The military troops are moving to the North, slowly taking over the entire Zone. What are they preparing for? And what will the second week bring us?
Military patrols
Military patrols are showing up in the most unexpected places — like someone’s moving figures across a chessboard.
There are no safe paths in the South any more: helicopters roar overhead, radio chatter hisses constantly, and soldiers can be around any corner.
But the North is not left out either. It seems the military found a way to get in there — rumour has it they struck some sort of deal with the Frontier. They have settled now: patrols are seen more frequently, and they’re reportedly stationed near the Barrier area.
Consumables increased prices
Attention, all Zone inhabitants! Military operations have severely disrupted supply lines — shipments from the Mainland are dwindling, and factions are already feeling the shortage. Prices are rising, and traders are feeling the pressure. If nothing changes, it won’t be anomalies that destroy us — it'll be inflation.
Consumable prices have increased across all locations (except the Swamps and Frontier Base):
• 
Roadside — +10%
• 
The Bar — +25%
• 
North faction bases — +50%
Thanks to the military, supplies at the Frontier northern base were not compromised.
The changes also affected Session Battles.
The price increase is temporary — once supply routes from the Mainland are restored, costs should normalize.
Temporary questlines
Gunfire echoes through Forge-11, helicopter blades slice the sky — the military has entrenched itself in the North. Everyone pretends to be in control, but no one truly understands what’s happening.
Each faction has its own version of the truth, its own deals, its own goals. Some are trading with the military, others are on a watch, many are just trying to survive. But there is one thing that unites all: a growing sense that there is something more behind this invasion.
What is the military really after? Why are they acting so cautiously — yet with unwavering resolve?
You’ll have to find the answers yourself. 
Temporary questlines are now available — unique for each faction. They unlock after completing the southern Call storyline. You’ve got two weeks to complete them.
In the line of duty (Frontier)
The Frontier is backing the ongoing operation. Erzhan has commanded to find someone to help establish a beachhead for the SSPP forces. Time to step up.
Our duty is to protect the Earth from the dangers of the Zone! The SSPP forces might be our best shot. Look for Dublekick at the Frontier base.
Military Targets (Mercenaries)
The Mercs have received intriguing contracts: eliminate key military officers and gather intel on their plans. Hurry to get your contract — these jobs are rare and well-paid!
For more information, contact Roger at Mercenaries base.
Exchange of knowledge (Rise)
Rise co-operates with the NBCP troops on mutually beneficial terms in an effort to unravel another mystery of the Zone. The Zone is a heritage for the entire population of the planet! If we can solve the next of its mysteries, there is nothing we will stop at. Neither prejudice nor old offences shall disturb our work! 
Major Granitsky suggests we exchange knowledge! Find him at the Rise Base.
Good Samaritan (Covenant)
Holy Covenant warriors seek to punish the sinners who have set foot on sacred ground in righteous fury, but have been defeated and disappeared. Covenant, your brothers, did not heed the Metropolite's words and vanished. Each one of our lives is precious and sacred. We must help them! We must save them! Yeremy is looking for help in the Covenant Base — don't deny him.
Improvement of the season tasks interface
We considered your feedback and improved the interface of season tasks: we fixed a number of bugs and made adjustments to make it more informative.
• 
Fixed bug with missing task counter for weekly bonus for non-premium players.
• 
Weekly bonus rewards can be manually claimed. This prevents confusion when awarding them.
• 
Improved readability of a number of inscriptions on the season tasks screen, they are now brighter and more contrasting.
• 
Daily rewards receiving button is now highlighted. Also, the texts on the button have been changed to make it more informative.
• 
Fixed a bug with incorrect display of time to task update for some players.
• 
Bills season currency is now activated immediately, without reaching the personal storage. Please note that before the update, some season currency could get to the personal storage.
• 
Fixed a bug that caused the list of tasks, categories, and locations available for tasks to flash when scrolling through categories.
• 
Centred the text of the category descriptions.
• 
Fixed the premium description on the season tasks screen and in the shop.
• 
Updated sounds in the season task menu.
• 
Other improvements and interface changes.
Fixes of information about tasks and subjects
• 
Added the Labyrinth to the Defence of Scientists from Mutants task as a suitable location for completion.
• 
Additional locations are listed for the Hunting the Behemoth task: Black Detour and Reflection.
• 
Expanded the list of locations to complete the Mutt Den task.
• 
Corrected the description of the Overdrive item.
Changes to daily tasks
Some tasks after the update caused bugs or created the possibility of receiving rewards unfairly, so they were removed:
• 
Ending the combats;
• 
Shooting at heads;
• 
Placing barricades.
Instead, there will be new tasks in the future! 
We have plans to keep adding and updating the list of activities, giving you the opportunity to earn Season Pass points for activities that don't currently give them.
Thanks to your ideas, we will continue to fix and improve the Season Pass.
In addition:
• 
A number of balance adjustments have been made, including reducing the number of required completions for a number of open-world tasks to earn rewards.
• 
Collecting Red Ferns is now counted for the Gathering bush plants task.
• 
Added a task for Northern players to clean up the Ghoul Den.
Bug fixes and other changes
• 
Fixed the movement distance of the fiend, dark ghoul, and behemoth.
• 
Fixed a bug that caused ghouls to attack a character with fire when attacking an Anomaly Research Installation.
• 
The Mercenary faction's daily quest to kill 15 enemies now counts new tasks.
• 
Fixed the appearance of the reward box for completing the Abandoned Outpost task at the Inflow location.
• 
Fixed the issue making outposts take a long time to appear.
• 
Removed open world activities erroneously awarding season points.
• 
For non-premium players, the number of available rerolls has been increased to 10.
• 
Updated the interaction sounds with Desert Eagle, its variants and the Business Approach style.
• 
Updated FN Fal, AK-15, SCAR SSR gunfire sounds.

historical_patches.title: Patchnote [18.06.2025]
historical_patches.text:
We've all got used to the grim atmosphere of the Zone, but it feels different now — tense and loud. S.S.P.P. soldiers are thoroughly examining every inch of the territory, clearly pursuing their own interests. Gunfire echoes across the Zone, confusion spreads. Their helicopters hover above anomalies, and their troops check every corner looking for something crucial. What are they really after? And why does it feel like this chaos is only the calm before the storm?
Events changes
After eruptions, neutral Outposts and Forge-11 Strongholds are now under S.S.P.P. control.
Consumables price changes
Prices are up again! Military forces are blocking supply lines. As a result, the third week brings us another 10% increase for consumables prices, including in session modes. Frontier is not affected by these changes.
Season Pass dailies changes
We continue refining daily tasks based on your feedback.
Combat
Reduced the number of completions required for the following tasks:
• 
Elimination of enemy sappers;
• 
Elimination of enemy Strike Groups;
• 
Clearing-out enemy camps.
Changes in categories
Exploration — reduced the required completions for the Dark Ghouls hunting task.
Science — increased the required completions for Collecting pulp and Gathering of minerals tasks.
Session modes
Added a headshot kill task on session modes.
We introduced it as an alternative for tracking the number of headshots, seeking to adjust the task so that it would be performed with approximately the same efficiency regardless of the type of weapon.
Returned the task to complete the session battles, but now with the requirement to score at least 1000 points to complete it.
Initially, we liked this task, but it provoked the appearance of players who simply went AFK to get the reward. Although such farming was not very effective, this behaviour had a negative impact on the experience of other participants. To prevent this, we have introduced a minimum score threshold to complete the task.
Subdivision battles
• 
Added a headshot kill task on Subdivision Battles;
• 
Reduced the number of required completions for the Eliminate enemies and Assist in killing enemies tasks;
• 
Reduced the amount of damage required in the Damage enemies and Damage enemy structures tasks;
• 
Reduced the number of points required in the Scoring for capturing points in subdivision battles and Scoring personal points in subdivision battles tasks;
• 
Removed the Reviving allies from knockdown in subdivision battles task.
The task turned out to be extremely rarely completed and rather took away the opportunity to effectively replace another task. In addition, it provided opportunities for abuse.
We would like to remind you that we are continuing to balance the Season Pass tasks and are also planning to add new ones! 
Compensation
Everyone who upgraded the temporary IATMS SSPP suit issued to complete the temporary quest chain for Rise will be refunded to the mail in a week.
Tasks changes
• 
Reduced grenade throwing range for sappers;
• 
Fixed a bug that caused not all items of the Red Fern type to count towards the Gathering bush plants task;
• 
Fixed a bug causing the Defending scientists from mutants task to appear for players who are not members of the Northern factions;
• 
Made adjustments and updates to a number of open world events;
• 
Fixed a number of daily faction tasks: fixed bugs that caused some new events to not count towards completion.
Interface fixes
• 
Fixed a bug that caused the time left to complete daily tasks to be displayed incorrectly;
• 
Fixed mistakes in the description of the premium.

Everyone in the North heard those terrible sounds — explosions, gunfire, screams… Military headed to Pripyat. But what will it change?

historical_patches.title: Special Case rework

On July 2, we’ll temporarily remove the Special Case from the game. The reason is simple: it’s hitting the in-game economy harder than an eruption hits a raincoat in Swamps. historical_patches.title: Patchnote [02.07.2025]
historical_patches.text:
Link to video overview of the patchnote with subtitles: YouTube
They say the Zone remembers a lot. But even it, with all its sinister memories, had forgotten what real military power meant. S.S.P.P. soldiers rushed into the Zone quickly and unceremoniously. They caused such a commotion that the stalkers fell silent on the frequencies, and even the mutants seemed to have retreated into their burrows.
And then came operation Pole. Assault on Pripyat. Almost no one saw it, but everyone heard it. Cannon fire shook the ground as if the Zone itself was groaning in pain. It began abruptly and, oddly enough, ended just as quickly. Everything went quiet. Radio only buzzed with fragments of negotiations. First came confidence, then panic, then…. emptiness. The familiar name Murmur was heard more and more often. People thought they had separated long ago, having fallen out with each other. And their resistance turned out to be not only successful, but also completely unexpected.
Rumours spread that the military had fled in disgrace. But later… someone let slip that they didn't leave empty-handed. 
At the same time, strange things began to be noticed in the north. Groups of silhouettes moving through the fog beyond the boundaries of accessible places — either fanatics or zombies. Fighters returning from night raids shared alarming observations that something unknown and massive was bypassing Forge-11. 
And then — disappearances. Experienced diggers disappeared one by one. Scientists hurriedly checked their instruments — seismographs showed spikes, but not the kind that indicate an eruption. Something else…
Attack on Perimeter season event 
How to play?
Players need to complete special missions in teams of three.
To start participating in missions, the player needs to select a direction in the event window: South or North.
The direction determines the set of main tasks that the player's squad needs to complete during the mission.
Then the player needs to select the difficulty level.
The higher the difficulty, the deadlier the enemies will be and the greater the rewards for successful completion.
The event features a system of modifiers that affect all game missions in the direction.
The system consists of both positive bonuses and negative debuffs.
Modifiers change every few days.
Participation in missions
Each mission involves three teams of three players.
Tasks:
• 
Complete the main tasks specific to each group;
• 
Successfully evacuate from the mission within a limited time — the final stage of Attack on Perimeter.
The list of main tasks is located on the right side of the screen.
The number of main tasks completed determines the players' reward in the session, as well as the percentage of the players' contribution to the success of the direction.
Teams can also perform additional tasks — all other events in the mission that are not related to the main objectives.
The number of additional tasks completed affects the final reward at the end of the mission for all players in the session.
Missions last for a limited time, and regardless of how successful you are at completing your tasks, the evacuation phase begins towards the end of the mission.
During evacuation, teams should:
• 
Successfully reach the helicopter landing site;
• 
Survive under the onslaught of the Murmur waves;
• 
Successfully evacuate.
Whether you evacuated or not determines the number of rewards you receive at the end of the mission.
Tactical support
On missions, S.S.P.P. soldiers don't send you empty-handed: each player is given a radio to call for tactical support.
There are three types of tactical support:
• 
Combat support — shelling, bombs, helicopter fire, etc.
• 
Supply — restocking ammo, meds, and armour plates.
• 
Special weapons — reinforced weapons used by S.S.P.P. soldiers, with unique features and high damage output.
In total, the player can choose a maximum of four tactical supports per mission. Therefore, we advise you to decide within your team who will restock the team's ammo and who will call in fire on the enemy!
To call for tactical support, the player must press the radio activation button (Q by default).
Then enter the support combination in two ways:
• 
By clicking the left and right mouse buttons, where the mouse buttons correspond to the directions of the arrows on the screen;
• 
By pressing the arrows on the keyboard.
After successfully entering the tactical support combination, it will be activated. It can be called up:
• 
The player needs to use the laser to aim by holding down the right mouse button;
• 
After pointing the laser at the spot where tactical support will be called, the player calls it by pressing the left mouse button.
After successfully calling for support, the military needs to refill its tactical support supplies, so it goes to recharge.
Keep this in mind so that you can call in tactical support at the right time and with maximum benefit. 
Military branches
Initially, players have access to only four basic tactical supports.
To unlock new ones, players need to level up military branches.
There are four branches in total:
• 
Logistics
• 
Scouting
• 
Artillery
• 
Aviation
Each branch unlocks its own types of tactical support and, in addition, gives passive bonuses to the player during missions, as well as bonuses for earning Dotations.
To level up branches, players need to earn Murmur Trophies, which come in three rarities: Common, Rare, and Unique.
You can get Trophies by:
• 
Completing the main and additional tasks;
• 
Founding on the ground during a mission.
The trophies collected by each squad are totalled at the end of the mission, and all players receive a shared reward.
Keep in mind that during the mission, trophies go into your inventory and drop when you die.
Rewards
For completing the mission, the player receives:
• 
Game rubles;
• 
Dotations — currency required to open special season event cases;
• 
Murmur trophies — items needed to level up branches.
The amount of the reward depends on:
• 
selected difficulty level;
• 
number of main and additional tasks completed;
• 
successful evacuation;
• 
contribution to the mission of other squads — the contributions of all squads in the session are summed up, and players receive a shared reward.
In the event of death, failure to complete main tasks, or unsuccessful evacuation, the player receives a reduced number of rewards.
In addition, successful completion of the mission contributes to the overall progress of the direction that determines the development of the plot of the Attack on Perimeter event.
So cooperate, make your personal contribution, and follow the story!
Attack on Perimeter cases
In battles with the Murmur, soldiers occasionally manage to capture crates containing advanced technology — Soldier's Crate, Officer's Stuff, Captain's Loot, and Colonel's Reserve.
They are located in Military Supplies and can be purchased from S.S.P.P. fighters for Dotations earned in Attack on Perimeter missions.
In these crates you can find:
New artefacts: Fossil, Gills, Hoop, Stress fest and Colophony.
The first samples have already been sent to scientists, who are busy studying and identifying its properties.
Master weapon attachments: Dystonia grip, Trapezoid collimator sight, Antithesis silencer, and Sciera laser sight in three variations.
In addition, playing Attack on Perimeter allows you to earn unique achievements. What are they? Find out by playing the game.
Twitch Drops store
The Dealer and Twitch Drops case have updated their assortment:
• 
Bastion paint (weapons and armour);
• 
Sharp paint (weapons and armour);
• 
Macula and Augmentation paints;
• 
Canned Ghoul and Mini Coil charms;
• 
Biomech skin.
Season Pass tasks rework
There were many problems in the previous iteration of the tasks:
• 
You had to constantly switch tasks in order to engage in activities you enjoyed;
• 
Many tasks had an unequal ratio of rewards to time spent;
• 
The mechanics of selecting categories were inherited from the old system and only complicated interaction with the new one.
We have taken all these issues into account and slightly rethought the Season Pass system. 
• 
Added sections for Open World and Session Modes;
• 
A special task mechanism has been introduced. Such tasks are counted as several.
For example, when capturing an outpost, the player now earns progress on the weekly and daily scales as if they had completed the regular task twice.
This includes the use of two Overdrives instead of one, if they are activated and the conditions for receiving the Overdrive reward are met.
Open World section
The categories Combat, Research, and Science have been removed. Instead, the following have been introduced:
• 
Basic open world activities. Tasks in this category do not require replacement — they are always available for completion.
The following tasks can be performed within this category:
• 
completing tasks from the announcement board and fraction assignments;
• 
completing any events in the open world;
• 
killing players in the open world;
• 
searching for signals, caches, artefacts;
• 
collection of shrub plants, minerals, and pulp;
• 
delivering backpacks.
 2. Completing events. Tasks in this category provide Season Pass points for completing specific events. Most of the tasks from the deleted categories have been moved here. Four tasks can be available in this category at the same time.
 3. Complex activities. This category contains special tasks, many of which earn as many Season Pass points as two or three regular tasks.
Selecting categories is no longer necessary — players now have access to all of the above open world task categories simultaneously.
Session Modes section
Includes the Session Battles and Subdivision Battles categories.
Added tasks counted as Complex Activities from the Open World section:
• 
complete the session battle with more than 10,000 points;
• 
take first place in Arms Race or DeathMatch;
• 
kill 6 people in one life in session battles;
• 
win the subdivision battle match;
• 
kill 5 people in one life in subdivision battles.
Added the event category Attack on Perimeter. 
All categories of Session Modes are available simultaneously — there is no need to choose between them or reject open world categories.
(Of course, provided that the following conditions are met: reaching level 5 in session battles, joining a subdivision, reaching the required safe zone, participating in the event.)
Added challenges — they are not counted towards daily and weekly tasks, but give a separate reward.
Please note that we will continue to modify the tasks — both to simplify and to complicate them. Balance is not final!
We also continue to closely monitor your feedback and improve the Season Pass system!
Advanced case
The long-awaited Advanced case is back. This time, it works the same way as Special, with one exception: the rewards start at the Veteran rank instead of Stalker. As before, the case is only available for a limited time: until 23 July.
This time, the unique item is the HK MP7A2.
You can also expect interesting offers in the form of the FN SCAR-H and the new Derya MK-12 AS-103S calibre 12 shotgun.
Hurry up and get the gear you want!
The Special Case that has been sent for rework will return later in the season. All chances earned will be saved.
Special pack
A new special offer is available in the in-game store — the SSPP support event pack. It includes Season Pass levels, Murmur trophy crates, Gift of Murmur crates, and Dotations.
Style at level 1000
At level 1000, a unique style is unlocked — Soulreaper. When killing with a weapon with this style, steam comes out of it.
The demo version of the Beretta ARX-160 in the hideout has been changed to the Soulreaper variant.
Barter update
New weapons added to the barter tree:
• 
LWRC M6;
• 
SIG516;
• 
KS-1.
The LWRC M6 has replaced the M4 CQC both in the barter tree and in players' hands.
For one month, the Dealer is offering a free exchange of L85 for LWRC M6 and vice versa.
Changes in session modes
• 
Added a new DM map, Glass, with themed equipment;
• 
In the Assault on the Streets of Pripyat session mode, Murmur fighters now wear the Soulreaper style on the Beretta ARX-160.
• 
The number of kills before changing weapons in the arms race has been increased to 3;
• 
The maximum duration of the arms race game has been increased to 8 minutes.
Other changes
Updated animations
• 
Added physical impulse when firing a lethal shot from a weapon at player and non-player characters;
• 
Disabled interruption of melee weapon inspection when starting a sprint;
• 
Added new zombie animations;
• 
Updated textures and paint mask for the M249 SAW.
Updated event HUD
The event HUD has been updated and now shows the number of remaining targets.
Fixed trade packs
Fixed the inability to rename a trade pack.
Premium rewards change
15 tasks — 1,000 bills; 
45 tasks — 2,000 bills; 
100 tasks — 2 Gift of Murmur season cases.
Season Pass task adjustments
Completing tasks during warm-ups in Session Battles and Subdivision Battles will no longer count towards your score.
First week of challenges
Added first challenges. They are not included in daily and weekly tasks and give a separate reward.

historical_patches.title: Hotfix [03.07.2025]
Patchnote [10.07.2025]
historical_patches.text:
Well, Seekers, the calendar shows July 10, which means it’s time to celebrate 11 years of our beloved game! 
First, we want to thank you for playing STALCRAFT: X. With your support, we’ve spent all these years building a unique world in the heart of the Exclusion Zone. 
May your bullets always hit the mark, behemoths get squished by you, and Elbrus sell for a good price! 
And we’ll keep working hard for you. Every day, a team of over 300 people builds and maintains this world — both in-game and beyond: chatting with you in the community and creating content. 
There’s a lot more we’d love to say, but we won’t keep you waiting. So let’s get to the good stuff — the celebratory update!
Years of Service
While thinking of ways to entertain and reward you, we went through all sorts of ideas — from crazy funny ones to just straight crazy. Here's our gift to you this year!
Triumphs system
To celebrate, we’re launching a triumphant new feature! A brand-new system is being introduced to the game that lets you earn valuable rewards, but you’ll have to work for them!
Last year, in honour of the anniversary, we rewarded our players with special items — their quantity and quality increased depending on how many years the player had been with us. The most loyal ones received Legacy SCAR-L and Longevity. This time, it’s not a milestone anniversary, so in addition to coins for Years of Service, we’re also taking into account how active you’ve been throughout the year. 
The Triumphs system allows to claim rewards from past years that players may have missed.
Unique challenges were added to the game that include different aspects of gameplay. Completing them grants access to a wide range of rewards, such as:
• 
The unique Trailblazer motif, wearable on three armours!
These include: ZIVCAS M2-C Armored Suit, Nord Group Guardian and Nord-22 Group Guardian, Albatross Heavy Assault Armored Exoskeleton.
• 
Longevity and Legacy SCAR-L: available again for those who missed them, though at a cost. 
A player who doesn’t have enough years spent in the game but is highly active will be able to earn just one of these rewards, if they really put in the effort. 
• 
 Beloved by many Tanto with a Ring is now reworked into a master rank version for those who asked.
Other rewards include:
• 
The deadly Gift for the Chosen One;
• 
A bundle of nice little extras and two mysterious cases. 
All of this will be available for purchase using the new, unique Pops Coins.
• 
Trailblazers Case contains a unique, mysterious master rank item for this year. Next year, it will become available for purchase with Pops Coins, but at a higher price than the case. 
We don’t know yet when this case will be opened. We’re still looking for a skilled master who can find the key!
• 
A Crate from the Forgotten Times contains character skins from pre-release times and earlier.
Wait, who's that? A veteran? A Session warrior? Target audience? That’s none other than the legendary Zone elder — Pop! You can find him at every safe zone except the Swamps and the Digger bases — he’s ready to offer you his selection of goods and share his story!
And if you complete all 10 Triumph challenges, you’ll unlock a personal muse waiting for you after raids in your personal hideout!
How to earn Pops Coins?
By using the promo code, which you'll get for our birthday. It will grant you a reward equivalent to your Years of Service. The number of coins in the promo code depends on when your account was registered.
The most curious players have already uncovered info from our developers about the new Triumph system and how to earn the new coins. This system works similarly to challenges. If you’ve already met the requirements between 2024 and now, the tasks will automatically be marked as complete — and you’ll be able to collect the rewards right away!
Note: Triumph progress isn’t limited and doesn’t have a final score. So go ahead and brag to your friends about how long you’ve avoided touching grass while evacuating from Lyubech-3.
How does coin earning work if I have multiple characters on one account?
The promo code can be activated once for each character on the account. However, coins and most rewards can only be earned on one character.
Special Pack
SC: X Birthday Set has been added to the shop. Inside, you’ll find a crate of beer for your hideout, marvellous paint, and most importantly — unique charms! 
One tracks how many players you've killed. The other tracks how many players you've killed without dying.

Aesthete Case I
The special pack isn’t the only new thing! Aesthete Case I is also now available in the shop. Inside:
• 
8 weapon motifs 
• 
2 motif series 
• 
A unique bolt skin Phase
Each time you pull Phase, it comes with a random embedded particle that changes the item’s visuals or animations — or both, if you’re lucky! 
You’ll have to find out what each particle does by playing the game.
All items dropped from the case are bound for 90 days. 
The case will be available for purchase until January 14. 
The mechanics are similar to the Special and Advanced cases, with increasing drop rates for non-standard items. But this case includes dupe protection: if you already pulled an item of standard rarity, it won’t drop again until you’ve collected all other motifs of the same rarity.
Golden tickets
On this special day, we traditionally thank the players who have made it into the top 50 sponsors of the project and present them with golden tickets. This ticket can be exchanged for a memorial gift from NPC Viv at the northern faction bases or at the Bar in the south. The gift includes both unique items for the game and valuable collectibles on the Mainland.
The personal promo code from this set holds a secret that will only be revealed in your hideout.
We guarantee that everyone will receive their gift from Vivy Wonka, but it will take some time.
Reward application form
The golden ticket will be sent to your in-game mail after server maintenance is over. After submitting your ticket to Viv, the reward application form will appear at the top of the stalcraft.net website. To receive an offline reward, you need to complete this form.
After completing the form, we will contact you from the official address delivery@exbo.net to confirm your details. Applications are processed individually and may take some time. The gift will then be sent by courier service at our expense.
Important: Beware of scammers!
• 
We will only contact you at the email address delivery@exbo.net or by telephone number provided in the form.
• 
Never share your account details.
• 
All expenses, including delivery, are fully covered by EXBO.
• 
If you have any questions, please contact technical support.
Transfers are only possible within one account. If the ticket was not sent to the main character, technical support will perform a one-time transfer.
Transfer to third-party accounts is not provided.
You can transfer a golden ticket for 10 and 11 years to Viv until 1 July 2026, 00:00 (GMT+3).
What about the 10-year reward?
This year, we have prepared golden ticket rewards for two years at once — for the 10th and 11th birthdays of STALCRAFT: X. And now we want to clarify why the distribution of gifts for the 10 years anniversary has been so delayed.
We spent a long time searching for a supplier, considering different shapes and materials for the figures. It is important to note that each figure is painted by hand, which significantly increases its shipping time. Our goal was to find the perfect figure that would not break after a week. We managed to do it, but the whole process from testing to approval took much longer than we expected.
Unfortunately, the preparation process is such that we cannot send gifts right now. Therefore, holders of golden tickets for 11 years will also have to wait a little longer, as some figures are still in production. To brighten up the wait for your long-awaited parcel, Viv will give you an in-game gift right now.
Sub-storylines
After the update, new story quests await you, revealing new details about the exciting events in the Zone!
Quest line Initiation for Covenant
Do the unfaithful deserve forgiveness? A second chance? Opportunities to become part of the Covenant? Help Tretyak recruit prisoners. Let them learn the truth of the Covenant — through suffering!
The quest becomes available after completing The Frontier of War task in the Sinfulness storyline, and new missions become available as you progress through the storyline.
Quest line Botwin’s Research for Rise
Professor Botvin set up an entire laboratory in the basement of the Institute for his research. You can work there as a lab assistant to find out… at what temperature your own brain will boil!
The quest becomes available after completing the Herschel task in the New Rise storyline, and new missions become available as you progress through the storyline.
Quest line Swiss’ Orders for Mercenaries
A certain Swiss man, one of Muller's loyal associates, is prepared to share several interesting contracts. But it's not that simple: some customers want their targets eliminated in a specific way.
The quest becomes available after completing the New Stage task in the A Mercenary's Honour storyline, and new missions become available as you progress through the storyline.
Quest line Den’s Guardian for Frontier
It's restless in the Den again. This time, Brazen declared a hunt for particularly dangerous creatures that interfere with the frontier guards at the Barrier. Help cleanse the Den from the Zone's creatures. It's time to fulfil your duty!
The quest becomes available after completing the Confrontation Inevitable task in the When Duty Calls storyline, and new missions become available as you progress through the storyline.

•

•

historical_patches.title: Patchnote [16.07.2025]
historical_patches.text:
Attack on Perimeter
Thanks to the dedicated actions of the S.S.P.P. military and the brave Seeker volunteers who displayed incredible cohesion and professionalism, the Attack on Perimeter event has successfully moved forward and tipped the scales on the side of S.S.P.P. Now the key events are unfolding on the territory of the Roadside — a place where now every step can become decisive. However, don't relax: Murmur's officers are not the type to give up without a fight. They are already adapting their tactics, arming their squads to the teeth and preparing for a massive war, eager to take their victory without regard for casualties. Tense battles, scorched earth and new challenges await you. They will require your utmost concentration and skill.
What's new:
New enemies — reinforced Murmur squads equipped with advanced weapons and technology.
New tasks — unique tasks related to defending and attacking key points on the Roadside.
Location change — dynamic environment with increased danger and new anomalies.
Prepare for the Roadside to become the battlefield where the fate of this entire operation will be decided. Check your gear, assemble your team and enter the fight — the time for action is now!
Shelf for shopping and case items
A new shelf for items bought from the Shop or items from cases.
We've taken your feedback into account, now styles don't clutter up the personal storage without a 90-day transfer option.
This shelf automatically holds all items that used to go into the personal storage when you bought them in the shop or opened a case. You can take any item from the shelf, but you can't put anything there. The shelf is only shown when something is lying there. When something appears on the shelf, it is indicated by a red marker on the shelf itself and on the button to go to the personal storage.
Overdriven pack and Overcharged charm
The Overdriven pack is available for purchase up to 3 times and contains:
• 
1 charm;
• 
50 overdrives.
If overdrives don't interest you — you can also purchase the charm separately.
Special case
We're returning the Special case to the game. For all players, the number of accumulated case openings required to obtain a guaranteed item is maintained at the level it was at the time the case was removed from the game. At the same time, item drop chances have been reviewed and adjusted to minimise any possible negative impact on the game's economy.
Session modes
Arms Race:
• 
Reduced movement speed from 40% to 20%.
• 
You can no longer deal damage in melee combat, except for the last stage, which grants a katana.
DM GOST-17:
• 
Changed equipment — now HK MP7A2 with a set of replaceable attachments is used as the main weapon and RSh-12 as a secondary weapon.
• 
The tactical katana on this map now gives no bonus to movement speed.
Other changes
Updated the models of the following inflators:
• 
CMMG SV Brake 7.62×51;
• 
Keeno Arms SHREWD 7.62×51;
• 
SureFire Pro Comp 7.62×51;
• 
Odin Works ATLAS 7.62×51;
• 
Sig Sauer SRD762Ti.
Fixed the Home turf motif that could not be installed on Arsenal's FAL.
There is now someone to look after the newbies on the Roadside bases.

historical_patches.title: Patchnote [23.07.2025]
historical_patches.text:
Attack on Perimeter
A malfunction in the Murmur gravitational beacon has triggered the spread of anomalies across the Roadside, leading to the regrouping of hostile forces. Enemy activity has intensified near the Kolos Agrocomplex and surrounding areas, threatening to cut off access to the military town.
Your objective:
Neutralize enemy groups in the Roadside and prevent their unification.
Time works against us.
Main direction
Due to the worsening situation, command has reinforced our forces. Captain Makarov has arrived to replace Colonels Zakharov and Kondratenko. All units previously involved in operations against the Murmur have now been unified under a single front.
Modifiers
The situation is escalating, all Murmur forces are regrouping, which has increased the pressure on allies.
The number of modifiers on the Lethal difficulty has reached six.

historical_patches.title: Patchnote [30.07.2025]
historical_patches.text:
The event loved by many came to an end! The S.S.P.P. military fired all their ammo, and the project team worked their fingers to the bone while making updates. You'll learn about a little Lyubech-3 rework, new signals, balance adjustments and a lot more. Let's dive into everything that awaits us in this patchnote!
The end of Attack on Perimeter
The loved-by-many funny event has come to an end.
Deleted Attack on Perimeter daily tasks and challenges, yet we left the opportunity to exchange your Murmur Trophies to Dotations to open Military Supplies cases for 2 more weeks.
The awards for those who've been noticed by the Big Brother will be sent later.
New offer at Exchanger
Our economists did their best to make the offers for six and seven parts of the legendary Albatross Heavy Assault Armored Exoskeleton and Gauss Rifle available without a heavy grind, but it's still not so easy to get:
Barter coupons do not apply for these offers!
Lyubech-3
Finally! Our devs finally made it up to our favourite location Lyubech-3. Although it is not yet the full rework, it will be released later. However, we hope these changes will meet your approval. And if not, don't forget to leave feedback with which we continue to improve our game!
Rework of the Location spawn system
Changed the Lyubech teleports placings on the domestic locations.
Similar to Labyrinth, only certain factions will face off at a location. The only difference is that Mercenaries will face Covenant, and Rise — Frontier.
Players now appear in the south of the location, which is divided into right and left zones, with one faction appearing on the left and the other on the right. Faction change these zones every 30 minutes. For example: if Mercenaries appeared on the right and Covenant on the left, they switch places after 30 minutes.
Added trampolines on the south location to speed the movements.
Lyubech-3 awards and events changes
• 
Significantly reduced weight of all the resources.
• 
Increased the resource reward from all events from 10% to 15%.
• 
Now, two bosses can be on the map at the same time.
• 
Now ID from bosses and the installations drops starting 10% damage to the boss.
• 
Reduced the number of waves required to protect an anomaly installation to two.
• 
Reduced dropped cargo delivery time from three minutes to two minutes.
• 
Reduced the time to capture a dropped load from three minutes to two minutes.
• 
Reworked all NPCs in events and patrols.
• 
Reduced the density of many events and patrols to make the location less overpopulated.
• 
Increased the spawn of Behemoth and Fiend, now they will be encountered more often.

historical_patches.title: Operations, or how we developed PvE content in SC:X
historical_patches.text:
Very soon, the anomalous barrier of “notapriority” will finally collapse, and the first Operation will make its way into the Exclusion Zone.
This will be our first full-fledged PvE content, and we’re planning to make it a permanent part of STALCRAFT: X.
And to be honest — we’ve been grinding away at this for the past few years. We’ve made countless mistakes, hit failure after failure, all for the sake of bringing back that legendary Bloodsucker Dungeon! Well… not exactly that one, but at least we’ve taken the first real step in that direction!
In this article, we’ll break down when and what you can expect from the first Operation, introduce a new type of endgame reward for completing it, and share a heartfelt story of how a small indie team tried their hand at PvE content.
Contents 
• 
Attempt 1 — Mausoleum
• 
Attempt 2 — Daily Operations
• 
Attempt 3 — Operation Misfire
• 
Attempt 4 — Operation Cryostasis
• 
The main problem and its solution
• 
Operation Breach
• 
Classes with abilities
• 
Lyubech-3 style map
• 
Point capture with a twist
• 
Unusual enemies
• 
Boss — Rat hunter
• 
Permit system with rewards
• 
Endgame reward — Modules
• 
When will it be playable?
Attempt 1 — The Mausoleum
Back in distant 2022, in one of the deserted corridors of the office, a developer stumbled upon an ancient chat thread on his phone. Inside — screenshots of the dungeons that were cut after the rework: Devora, Toxic Snork, Rat hunter. He walked to the window with his phone, stood there thinking for a long time, shed a tear...
And then he decided — this couldn’t go on any longer! That very moment marked the formation of the first small team of enthusiasts, united by a single goal: to bring PvE back into the game.
For the first prototype, they chose the Mausoleum as a base. It was a repeatable, solo, dungeon-like quest that had been endlessly resurrected post-rework. But it kept breaking so often that it was never even released for players in the EU, NA, and SEA regions.
First prototype of Mausoleum
Initially, the team had no intention of changing the concept — the idea was simply to refresh the gameplay inside the dungeon. The plan was straightforward: 
• 
Use the existing map.
• 
Give the NPCs more up-to-date gear.
• 
Add an arena with a unique boss at the end. 
Seemed solid enough, but after the very first playtest, it became clear: the map was hopelessly outdated, and the NPCs (boss included) — felt no different from the enemies you'd already fought countless times in regular quests. 
Put simply: it was boring. Even the story dungeons in the South played and looked better.
Playtests are sessions where real players test mechanics or systems to identify bugs, check balance, and evaluate the overall gameplay experience for future improvements.
Second prototype of Mausoleum
After the failure of the first prototype, the team decided to shift the direction of development entirely: 
“If we can’t make the NPCs interesting, we need to try spicing things up with objectives and co-op”.
Around the same time, the team remembered that a few unused dungeon segments had been left behind after the release of the Southern storyline. Without overthinking it, they based the second Mausoleum prototype on a cut section of the Trailblazers’ Laboratory and outlined the following plan:
• Add the ability to run the dungeon in a squad.
• Assign a random main objective for each run.
• Introduce more random elements: blocked or open passages, shuffled locations for key items.
The gameplay immediately felt much more engaging. However, the Trailblazers’ Laboratory just wasn’t built for co-op, and the engine began to buckle under the weight of all the randomised dungeon elements. More and more bugs started piling up.
Naturally, there were no ready-made fixes for any of this — so continuing development, or even just maintaining the dungeon, became extremely painful...
The outcome of Mausoleum development
As a result, the Mausoleum was cancelled, and the team of enthusiasts was reassigned to develop the first Inside Out.
However, this initiative led to several important conclusions:
• The engine needs proper preparation.
• Separate maps must be created specifically for the mode.
• Even with dull enemies, players can be entertained with interesting objectives.
Attempt 2 — Daily Operations
After the Mausoleum, a different team of bold warriors decided to try and bring back the Bloodsucker dungeon creating a full-fledged PvE mode with a flashy name: Daily Operations.
It was at this point that the very first seeds of the Operations, soon to appear across the Exclusion Zone, were planted.
The first prototype of Daily Operations
The first prototype borrowed ideas from the Mausoleum but with some key differences:
• Removed the need to run to the dungeon by adding a session-based entry.
• Introduced increasing rewards based on how quickly you completed the dungeon.
• Added modifiers to boost variety and difficulty of gameplay.
For example, there was a planned modifier for increased gravity, forcing players to conserve stamina and think twice before jumping.
On top of that, Operations were designed to be daily — with not only rewards and objectives refreshed every day, but modifiers too.
But unfortunately, back then the development approach was rather chaotic, and no one could be spared to actually build the gameplay part of Daily Operations.
The team ended up waiting so long that they managed to finish all the interfaces and the map — complete with final visual polish.
In the end, no hands were ever freed up to actually develop the first prototype, so Daily Operations were put on ice — to be revisited once a proper team of game designers was in place and fully established.
The second prototype of Daily Operations
Unfortunately, MMO development never stands still — and any shelved content visibly withers before the developers’ eyes.
When the team tried to evolve the location’s gameplay into something more than simple point capture or defence objectives, it became clear: it would be easier to start from scratch than to rework a fully finished location.
The same applied to the interfaces. While they sat unused, a new visual style had already taken shape — meaning the old interfaces, realistically, also needed to be replaced.
The outcome of Daily Operations development
As a result, the decision was made to put development on hold temporarily and shift focus towards other updates — including early concepts for the North, in preparation for Day X.
As for the takeaways… Beyond the obvious ones:
• Building a mode within a single ecosystem is a solid approach.
• Modifiers were recognised as a necessary part of the mode.
These two lines still haunt us in our nightmares:
• Release content in some form — or risk never releasing it at all.
• Don’t build interfaces and maps without core gameplay, or the work risks being wasted. 
Attempt 3 — Operation Misfire
After development on the North began, one of the developers had a sudden thought: “Why don’t we make a shorter version of Daily Operations, so players aren’t left without content while the major update is in the works?”
And it made sense! That’s how Misfire was born — and, skipping ahead for a moment, it became the most ambitious Operation to date.
This time, alongside the best ideas from earlier Operation prototypes, several mechanics were also borrowed from Crow Arena:
• Depending on the suit worn, players were assigned a class with unique consumables and grenades.
• Players used the Lift to move between arenas, similar to Crow Arena.
• Each arena spawned enemies and gave a random objective.
• The final arena featured a boss. Defeating it meant a successful run.
• With each successful replay, players could unlock new difficulty levels, introducing modifiers and more valuable rewards.
On top of that, an updated enemy AI, originally intended for release with the North, was also integrated into this Operation, bringing full enemy classification into the mix.
And the cherry on top? The most valuable reward type planned: Modules.
Lift — a narrative element in Operations that allows temporary travel between sealed laboratories in the Zone.
The outcome of Operation Misfire development
To say the mode spiralled out of control would be an understatement… And to think — we only wanted to make a shorter version so players had something to play.
In the end, the first rushed prototype of Misfire was plagued with bugs, unfinished features, outdated visuals, and tiny arenas.
The final nail in the coffin was a defeat at the hands of the anomalous barrier known as “notapriority”. At that time, all development priority had shifted to Day X — and every available hand had to be redirected to the global update.
Fortunately, most of the groundwork didn’t go to waste. Misfire's locations were repurposed for the Northern storyline, class grenades made their way into Hideout crafting, and Modules (in a reworked form) were added to the Dead Man’s Marathon.
Attempt 4 — Operation Cryostasis
In the team’s view, all previous attempts had hit a dead end. That’s why Cryostasis was designed as a major rethinking of dungeon design in STALCRAFT: X. 
Randomisation had made development more difficult and the effort spent on it wasn’t improving content quality, just increasing the quantity.
So the decision was made to go for a linear dungeon, one that would focus players’ attention on co-op and engaging enemies:
• Classes were given active and passive abilities, deepening teamplay.
• Thanks to the linear structure, much more time could be spent polishing the map.
• Enemies became more varied, and they too gained unique abilities.
• At the same time, the ability to unlock new difficulty levels, along with which modifiers appeared, was also preserved.
From a narrative standpoint, alongside Lifts, Areas were introduced — testing grounds hiding unknown threats and long-forgotten technologies.
The outcome of Operation Cryostasis
And it felt like this was finally it. We’d come such a long way, learned from so many mistakes, and this time we even had a proper release date locked in… We’d built an entire winter season around the launch of the Operation!
But, as is often the case in game development, no matter how good it looks on paper, you only find out how it actually plays during the tests.
And the playtests showed exactly that: Cryostasis gameplay felt unshaped, the new large-scale map came with equally large-scale problems — and so on, and so forth. You’ve heard this tune before.
The main problem and its solution
It was only by refusing to give up and repeatedly smashing our heads against the wall that we finally understood why none of the dungeons ever made it to release — and more importantly, what had to be done to fix it.
The core problem was simple: we lacked both the tools and the experience to create the kind of engaging gameplay we’d actually be happy with.
For most of its history, STALCRAFT: X — or rather, STALCRAFT as a whole — had been focused entirely on PvP. None of us had any idea how many challenges we’d face trying to release something beyond just a standard set of story dungeons.
So, to break this cycle and finally overcome the “notapriority” curse, we chose to start small. We made PvE content a top priority, built a separate, fresh team around that goal — and now, they’re ready to show you where that path has led.
Operation Breach
Introducing Operations — a PvE mode for three players, where you’ll explore Areas hidden deep within the Zone and hunt down lost technologies.
More about the Areas, the Lift, and why ZIVCAS operative Phil is so obsessed with them — you’ll find out in the introductory Operations quest.
In short, Breach is a classic dungeon featuring point capture, a “hot potato” mechanic, unusual enemies with special abilities, and a unique boss at the finale.
Additionally, Operations introduce a class system with defined roles, infinite difficulty scaling, several gameplay-altering modifiers, and a new endgame reward in the form of Modules. But let’s take it step by step...
By the way, we shared some interesting information in the third Developer Diaries, so we recommend checking them out for a complete picture! At the moment, only subtitles are available. In the future, we will add a voiceover to this video.
Classes with abilities
Before the Operation begins, you’ll be assigned a class with unique abilities based on the suit you’re wearing. There are three classes available:
Assault — a combat-focused class designed to soak up damage and protect teammates.
Support — a scientific suits class focused on healing and assisting teammates.
Operative — a combo suits class designed for stealthy, high damage output.
As you can see, our class system follows the classic trio: tank, healer, and damage dealer (DPS). Each player picks one role to overcome the Zone’s challenges together.
That doesn’t mean tanks or healers can’t dish out damage effectively. It’s more about an additional gameplay focus than a strict division of duties!
Lyubech-3 style map
In the first Operation Breach, you’ll be dropped into one of the districts of the ghost town Lyubech-3. We’ll keep the role of the Murmur in this place a secret — as they say, “discover it through gameplay.”
That said, from a visual standpoint, we’ve packed the location with as many details as possible to highlight the Murmur's everyday life and the mystical atmosphere of a lost city.
By wandering through this Area-0 and examining a small part of the town up close, you’ll get a glimpse of what the revamped Lyubech-3 will look like in the future.
Point capture with a twist
At the start of the Operation, you’ll be tasked with capturing points guarded by the Murmur.
When designing the map, we paid special attention to enabling constant interaction and support between teammates.
However, closer to the middle, the point capture turns into a game of “hot potato”. The concept is simple:
• Capture points with “attractors” to charge anomalous batteries.
• Pick up the charged batteries.
• Carry them to the generator.
But there are a few twists. Due to strong anomalous radiation, the batteries are extremely sensitive to the environment and quickly lose their charge when out in the open.
Also, as soon as you pick one up, normal movement and the use of abilities become impossible. The only effective way to transport the battery is by passing it from player to player until it reaches the generator — very much like a game of “hot potato”.
Unusual enemies
You may have noticed that with each new event, NPCs became less like damage sponges and started exhibiting increasingly complex behaviour.
Throughout this time, we’ve been continuously improving them, and we can now say that NPC AI has reached a new intermediate stage!
This was especially crucial for Operations because, unlike PvP, where players create countless unique situations themselves — in Operations that heavy burden falls on the “computer”.
We developed new behaviour patterns, added unique abilities, and did everything possible to ensure PvE enemies present tough challenges, while your gear and class choice allow multiple ways to overcome them.
Creating and balancing enemies became one of the most demanding parts of development. But we’re not stopping here — we intend to keep refining the foundation to make the gameplay even more engaging!
Boss — Rat hunter
At the finale of Operation Breach, you’ll face off against the Murmur's boss — the Rat hunter. As his callsign suggests, he commands rats in battle against his enemies.
We won’t spoil the full details of the encounter, but we can say this: we aimed to make him more than just a stationary target. Expect a challenging opponent with a mix of active and passive abilities, unique attacks, and multiple phase transitions.
Permit system with rewards
Throughout the entire development of the mode, our main goal was to make it accessible to the vast majority of players.
That’s why we created the Access system — so that nearly anyone can jump into Operations, while the true legends of the Zone still get their dose of challenge.
Initially, to unlock access to Operation Breach, all you need is to reach the Pervomayskiy Factory Bar and complete the introductory quest. However, after each successful run, you’ll earn rewards and depending on your completion time — increase your Access level by one to three tiers, which directly affects the difficulty of the Operation.
To go into more detail: NPCs will deal more damage, have more health, and the overall conditions of the Operation may shift based on modifiers, which rotate every week.
It’s important to note that difficulty progresses steadily and can keep increasing almost endlessly — right up until players physically can’t beat a given Access level.
Naturally, the higher your Access level, the more valuable the rewards.
However, to make the reward system feel more dynamic and not force you to wait for months — we’ve added weekly rewards in addition to the immediate loot you get after each Operation. Your weekly reward depends on the highest Access level you reached during the past week.
On top of that, the more Operations you complete in a given week, the more options you’ll have when choosing your weekly rewards.
Endgame reward — Modules
Speaking of rewards! To increase the significance of Operations, we’ve introduced a special reward: Modules.
Module is a new type of attachment, usable exclusively on weapons with a +15 upgrade level. It can significantly alter a weapon’s behaviour — either by tweaking its stats or introducing entirely new mechanics.
Modules come in varying quality tiers and include a set of randomised parameters from three different categories. Unlike artefacts, however, they don’t require potential upgrades.
They mark our first real step towards STALCRAFT: X’s endgame rewards, offering nearly endless progression. We also plan to regularly expand the system with new mechanics going forward.
When will it be playable?
Operation Breach is the debut release from our new PvE team — and right now, your feedback matters more than ever. It’ll help us shape the future of the mode and decide where to focus next.
To collect feedback, we’re launching an Open Test Server (OTS) available to everyone in all regions, including Steam players. All you’ll need to do is select the STALCRAFT: X launch option in Steam.
And the obvious question — “When is the OTS going live?” — “This August!”
OTS will give us a chance to catch bugs, tweak balance, and polish every aspect, so by launch, you’ll be able to grind Module Cores smoothly and get the most out of the new mode.
After release, we won’t be slowing down. We'll keep refining the Operation based on your feedback — and that’s not just talk. Just like we did with the Season Pass rework, we’ll keep at it until the end result satisfies both you and us.
Only once we hit that goal will we shift back to developing new PvE content — with more dungeons and a few unexpected surprises already in the works.
Until then, we’ll be waiting for you on the OTS!
