historical_patches.title: Patch Notes [30.09.2026]
historical_patches.text:
Content
• 
Ticketopia Event
• 
End of Electrostorm
• 
Working Man’s Cut on NA server
• 
1000 level style — Air Seller
• 
New quest — Shock wave 
• 
Economy, rewards and progression
• 
Modification window update
• 
Making Safe Zone more lively
• 
Balance changes
• 
Other changes and fixes
Ticketopia Event
In autumn, not only leaves fall from the trees, but also Act Tickets, which can be obtained for PvE challenges or for challenges in the Coliseum. The event will run from October 14 to 28.
There will be 16 challenges in the event, 8 for each format. You can complete them in any combination: either 8 in PvE, or 8 in the Coliseum, or 4 and 4.
Locations to complete PvE challenges
They are only available in the North, Wild North and Lyubech-3. Challenges will not be completed in the peaceful South. Also, the reward does not depend on the selected location.
What challenges will there be
• 
PvE: only open-world activities not tied to direct competition with other players. Outposts, airdrops, and installations in the Wild North do not count.
• 
Coliseum: destroying enemy squads, capturing installations, activating rifts, and other tasks.
The remaining challenges will be announced when the event begins.
Rewards
For each completed challenge, a small reward is given. Larger rewards are granted for reaching certain milestones of completed challenges:
• 
2 challenges: 100 Act Tickets
• 
4 challenges: 150 Act Tickets
• 
6 challenges: Veil style for Albatross Interceptor. 
• 
8 challenges: 250 Act Tickets
To claim the main prizes, you only need to complete any 8 out of 16 challenges, freely mixing both formats.
End of Electrostorm
The event has come to an end. The styles that were obtainable during the event can now be sold to Zen in exchange for season currency.
Working Man’s Cut on NA server
Honest workers deserve honest rewards. A new event where ordinary North hard workers can get everything they're owed for the work they do every day.
At Mines, Inflow, Black Detour and Reflection events yield 20% more income — signals and stashes appear 20% more frequently as well. And don't forget about deliveries: even light cargo is valued three times higher.
Challenges can only be completed at Mines, Inflow, Black Detour and Reflection.
Completing challenges rewards you with anomalous serum and other valuable resources. This event is planned to run regularly, and your activity and feedback can influence this.
1000 level style — Air Seller
It's unknown how much the crafter loved Belyaev's books, but that's exactly what he named his creation.
The gun reliably produces an air base, enough to subdue enemies without using gunpowder. Those lucky ones who held it says it coughs slightly — something the gunsmith always denies.
New quest — Shock wave 
Gunfire can be heard near the base — right at the walls! Who could it be? The answer to this question will drag you into a whirlwind of industrial espionage and intrigues among the big players. And as everyone knows, the most unpleasant secrets are hidden under the biggest carpet. Like what happened at Forge-11 when the sky began to fall...
Economy, rewards and progression
We've reworked the reward system and economy to make progression across locations more tangible and strengthen the position of the Faction North. Certain activities have also received a significant reward buff. 
Now you're farming more than before. Here's why:
Previously, inventories got clogged with junk — small items took up space and were worth almost nothing.
According to the analytics data, players did not claim nearly half of the event rewards due to their low value and excess inventory space.
We've reworked rewards on the Faction North, aligning them ideologically with Wild North rewards. Fillers now take up less space and are worth more — the value of a player's inventory relative to its weight has increased.
Let's show the numbers using Mines as an example: 
Let’s say you came to a location and cleared 100 events: previously, just under half of the items awarded as rewards for clearing events were of extremely low value. As a result, receiving them was often seen more as a burden than a useful reward: players frequently sent such items to the Trash to avoid taking up inventory space.
With the update to the reward pool, the value of the items awarded will increase, making it worthwhile for players to collect each one.
The tables below show the results of our calculations for two scenarios: under current player behavior, where low-value items are not collected, and after the reward system is changed, when players will collect all awarded items.
Mutants — previously loot occupied 66 inventory slots and was worth 152 thousand. Now it takes 49 slots and is worth 351 thousand. Less space, more money.

Changes to the melee weapon specifications card
• 
The correct damage values for the quick strike were added to the stats card (previously, the data for the normal strike was incorrectly duplicated there).
• 
Added the Attack speed parameter (equivalent to rate of fire), which shows the number of strikes per minute for each attack type.
Armor
A new visual parameter, Size, was added to the armor stats, displaying the size of the equipment's hitbox. The mechanics and hitbox sizes themselves remain unchanged. The change applies only to the interface.
Weapons and interface
• 
The Type parameter, which specifies the slot for mounting the weapon, was added to the basic characteristics.
• 
Removed the redundant button for switching between base and summary metrics. Instead, a convenient toggle was added to the full stats card, which displays all previously hidden parameters (these are affected by installed attachments, anomalous modules, the upgrade level, and the type of ammunition).
• 
In the Codex comparison, you can now choose to compare weapons based on all their characteristics.
• 
The visual part of the comparison is updated: compact, easy-to-read arrows are now used instead of bulky scales.
• 
The display of anomalous modules in the general characteristics is now more compact, and the design of the module cards themselves is also updated.
Containers and infections
• 
The container properties now display infection limits. Once these limits are exceeded, infections begin to accumulate. The system's logic remained unchanged: the limit depends on the character's base protection and the container's internal protection.
Display of infections
For convenience and ease of understanding, the baseline infection rates are adjusted to -10. All damage, including armor and medical item damage, is multiplied by 20.
The logic behind how the parameters work has not changed in any way.
There is no need to reassemble the builds, the changes are purely visual.
Consequently, the threshold value for preventing the accumulation of infection in the container is now 10 instead of 0.5, and 20 instead of 1 for cold.
Other changes and fixes
• 
Added charm mount to the SPAS-15.
• 
Now, when you drag and drop attachments in the inventory, the weapons they can be equipped on are highlighted.
• 
Reworked the first-person animation system. If you notice that animations are behaving incorrectly or that sounds are missing from actions where they should be present, please report this to Support team.
• 
Adjusted the hand position on the AEK-965 with the grip installed.
• 
Fixed a delay in the crosshair's movement when entering aim mode.
• 
Added the ability to install grips on the MP-155 Ultima.
• 
Fixed an issue that prevented users from retrieving multiple emails at once using the Claim Selected button.
• 
Corrected several minor localization bugs in all languages.

historical_patches.title: Festivity OTS
historical_patches.text:
In this article, we’ll explain what OTS is, and how to test the Festivity event.
What is OTS?
OTS stands for Open Test Server. Here, you gain access to early versions of updates.
This time, it is open for EU and RU players only.
Your task is to provide feedback to help us identify and fix issues before the final release.
On the OTS, your character will have the gear they had at the moment they were added to the testing participant list.
Progress is not transferred between servers, and everything you do with items on OTS stays there.
Participants list
Access to the OTS will be granted to a limited number of players who reached the Bar reputation level 2 and played more than 10 hours last month.
How do I know if I have access?
EXBO launcher users will see a separate server available for download — STALZONE OTS.
Steam players can check for an in-game message titled “OTS invitation”, sent by System to their most recently active character. If you don’t have this message, you are not eligible for testing.
Testing period
OTS will run from October 23, 2026, 15:00 (UTC) to October 25, 2026, 20:59 (UTC).
Please note! This is a test server. It may be stopped or restarted for changes anytime.
What we're looking for on this OTS?
We want to hear your thoughts on the mode’s gameplay, economy, and balance.
All OTS testers will have access to a survey about Festivity event.
To participate in the survey, please open your in-game mail on the test server and select the "OTS survey" message.
We are counting on your feedback. You can also discuss the event tests on our Discord server in the discussion.
Please be understanding of any issues and not finished parts. We will monitor and maintain OTS until it ends.
How to start playing on OTS?
OTS will be available to players in RU and EU regions. Steam login remains supported.
If you’re using the launcher and have access, the server will automatically appear in your download list.
To join via Steam, you need to choose the available beta version in the game settings.
Important note! In Steam, the beta version is available for download to everyone, even those who were not included on the participant list.
This could lead to a situation where you waste bandwidth downloading but are unable to participate in testing.
To avoid this, we recommend using the EXBO Launcher to log into the test server, even if you usually play through Steam.
Detailed instructions are available here.
What should you do on the OTS?
Open the ESC menu, go to the Festivity tab, and click Play to start the match.
More about the event
Festivity is a PvPvE event where a team of five players must defend their Relic — a structure located in the center of the arena.
The match is divided into rounds:
• 
In the first three rounds, you’ll fight waves of mutants and NPCs;
• 
In the fourth round, you’ll face a boss;
• 
Every fifth round, you’ll face an opposing team. The team that deals more damage to the structure in the center of the map wins the round.
All players start the match without any gear and with 100 coins to spend in the shop (press “E”). You’ll start with low-tier armor and weapons and can upgrade your gear as the match progresses.
You’ll earn coins for completing rounds. The shop offers several armor and weapon options, as well as special Talismans with different stats.
Talismans can be combined into sets that provide additional bonuses. To complete a Talisman set, you need to use different Talismans from the same set rather than duplicates.
Besides buying gear, you can also spend coins to refresh and upgrade the shop. The higher the shop level, the more Talismans you can place in your container and the higher the chance of finding higher-tier gear.
You’ll learn more about the event while testing it. In your feedback, you can also let us know how clear or confusing you found the different game mechanics.
I found a bug, how can I report it?
Any issues discovered during testing can be reported to our Support:
https://support.exbo.games/en
For your convenience, you can also refer to the guides:
• 
Creating and filing a ticket
• 
Bug report of the game mechanics
• 
Bug report of the game world map
• 
Bug report of another kind of bug
• 
Bug report of the game quest
OTS challenges and rewards
To receive rewards, complete tasks in the Open Test Challenges tab of the Event Hub.
Rewards for successfully completed challenges will be sent to the main server and credited to the appropriate characters within 30 business days after OTS ends.

Here’s how progression will work
The progression mode will unlock on November 4 and remain available until the event ends on November 18. The mode will be available from 10:00 AM to 12:00 AM server time.
The first five leagues are fixed. You can earn points for both wins and losses in them.

historical_patches.title: Patch Notes [28.10.2026]
historical_patches.text:
Festivity
Festivity is a PvPvE event in which a team of five players must defend their Relic from waves of mutants and zombies, fight bosses, and face off against another team. Everyone starts the match with no gear and levels up as they go, buying and upgrading equipment along the way.
The event is available to players who have reached Bar reputation level 2.
How to play?
The team's main objective is to defend the Relic, which stands in the center of the PvE Arena.
A match is divided into rounds that play out in the following order:
• 
3 PvE rounds, in which you fight waves of mutants and zombies. The maximum damage your Relic can take during one round is 15%.
• 
A boss round. Every boss has unique abilities, so stay alert!
• 
A PvP round, in which you face the opposing team. The team that deals more damage to the Altar, the structure in the center of the map, wins. The losing side's Relic takes 10% damage.
An important feature of the PvP arena is bioinfection on the lower floor of the location. Only players in Scientist armor can stay in areas with level 4 bioinfection. Players in Combo armor can only stay in areas with level 2 and 3 bioinfection. Everyone else will have to attack the Altar from the upper position.
The maximum number of rounds in a match is 25.
From round 6 onward, modifiers are active in the match. They change every round and make your life harder.
From round 11 onward, two modifiers are active at the same time.
The match ends if:
• 
One team's Relic is completely destroyed;
• 
The players reach round 25. In that case, the team whose Relic has more durability remaining wins;
• 
One of the teams surrenders. Surrender button becomes available after round 15. Activating it starts a vote. If all team members agree, the team is defeated.
The button can be found in the bottom left corner when you open the match statistics with ~ key.
Shop and gear
All players start the match with a knife, a pistol, and 100 coins. This currency is called Yav. It's used in the shop to buy armor, weapons, and Amulets, as well as to upgrade and refresh the shop.
Yav is earned by completing rounds. The amount you receive depends on several factors:
• 
In a regular PvE round: how much Relic durability was lost;
• 
In a boss round and in a PvP round: whether you win or lose;
• 
How many coins you have from the previous round. 
The more Yav you have before the next round starts, the more bonus coins you'll get. For every 10 coins in hand at the end of a round, you receive +1 coin, up to a maximum of 30 coins.
You can see the bonus coin details by hovering over the Yav icon in your inventory.
Before each round, you get time to prepare and shop. The shop is built into your inventory. You can open it with the E key.
Several armor and weapon branches are available. Each armor type has its own characteristics:
• 
Combat armor is great for holding back enemy attacks, but prevents you from going down to the lower level of the PvP arena. It uses fragmentation grenades.
• 
Combo armor can withstand level 2 and 3 bioinfection (at higher armor ranks) in parts of the lower level of the PvP arena. It uses healing grenades.
• 
Scientist armor allows you to go down to the Altar and survive level 4 bioinfection. It also uses a shield grenade that blocks bullets.
Gear upgrade
To assemble higher rank gear, you need to purchase three of its blueprints.
Blueprints matching your current gear are highlighted in the shop.
All items in the shop are limited in quantity and are drawn from a shared pool. If you purchase one of the blueprints, it disappears from the shared pool. If you later sell it, it becomes available to everyone again.
Gear blueprints can also be used to upgrade armor or weapons to +5 and +10. To do this, purchase the required blueprint, then press Shift + LMB or drag it from your inventory into the equipment window.
After purchasing the third blueprint, the gear will automatically upgrade to the next rank.
Keep in mind that gear can only be upgraded in the correct order — from Picklock or Newbie to Master. You cannot upgrade Newbie armor or weapons straight to Master rank, skipping the Stalker and Veteran ranks!
• 
The maximum available rank for armor and primary weapons is Master.
• 
The maximum available rank for secondary weapons is Legendary.
If there is no items you need in the shop, you can refresh it for 10 Yav.
If the item you need appears in the shop but you can’t afford it yet, lock the shop by clicking the lock icon in the upper-right corner. In this case, the current set of items will be saved and carried over to the next round.
Shop upgrade
Yav can be spent not only on gear, but also on increasing the shop’s level. The higher its level, the higher the chance of finding higher-rank gear blueprints and the more Amulets you can equip.
Amulets
Amulets — are artifacts with special stats that can be purchased in the shop.
Each Amulets belongs to one of the following sets: Skitter, Fiend, Ghoul, Rat, or Multiset.
A set consists of three different artifacts and provides additional bonuses.
You can learn more about each set’s effects in the dedicated inventory tabs.
Note! A set only works with different artifacts from the same collection. If you buy two completely identical Amulets, the set's additional effect will not activate.
Multiset is a special Eti Amulet, that can work with any other set.
Amulets can be upgraded up to +15. To do this, find and buy another identical Amulet and combine it with the first one.
Rewards
At the end of a match, you'll receive rubles and Chrismites, the event currency.
Chrismites can be spent in the event shop on various rewards, including: 
• 
5.45 Extended Magazine;
• 
Athame hunter's knife;
• 
Myron, Death Knell, Crimson styles;
• 
Hideout decorations;
• 
Implements event case;
 Magazine, knife, decor and styles can be sold to Zen for event currency.
• 
Various consumables.
Progression
Access to the progression mode will open on November 4 after maintenance, and it will remain active until the end of the event on November 18. 
Progression mode will be available from 10:00 (server time) to 00:00 (server time).
Progression consists of leagues. Up to the Epiphany league, you'll earn points for both wins and losses, but fewer for a loss.
Rewards can be claimed immediately after you move from one league to the next. 
In addition to rewards for reaching new leagues, you’ll also receive extra Chrismites for reaching certain milestones.
In the Epiphany and Deliverance leagues, points are deducted for a loss. Rewards for reaching these leagues are only issued after the event ends.
Only 10% of players who reach league 5 will enter the Epiphany league, while the Deliverance league will include limited number of players with the highest number of points:
• 
EU — 90,
• 
NA — 15,
• 
SEA — 10,
• 
NEA — 10.
A case containing personal styles from previous Arenas is one of the rewards in the Epiphany and Deliverance leagues.
The reward in the case can be rerolled up to 8 times. Each reroll costs 5 million rubles. Duplicate items will not drop, so you are guaranteed to receive any style you want.
Tokens
Double progression tokens will let you climb the leagues faster. They can be purchased in the shop or obtained from Implements event case.
However, use them wisely in the Epiphany and Deliverance leagues: alongside the potential reward, the risk of losing more points also increases!
You can use up to 3 tokens per match. Depending on how many you use, the following multiplier is applied to the points you earn:
• 
1 token: ×2;
• 
2 tokens: ×2.6;
• 
3 tokens: ×3
In the Festivity event, tokens will only be active during the event and will be converted into Trade coins once it ends. This will help maintain fair competition and balance in each mode.
Challenges
Added Festivity challenges to the Season Pass.
You can find even more challenges and rewards in the event's dedicated tab.
Spend your weekends at Festivity!
From November 7, 05:00 (server time) to November 9, 05:00 (server time), and from November 14, 05:00 (server time) to November 16, 05:00 (server time), matches will earn 30% more rubles and Chrismites.
Don't miss the moment when the Zone is merciful and rewards suffering.
Safe Zones decorations
Residents of safe zones have started putting their own spin on the usual deserted corners… Come take a look!
New season quests
tulpa! season quests
This fall, the Zone faced a primal horror for the first time. Each faction follows its own path in the hope of defeating it: some seek salvation in science, while others seek it in rituals. Fire and Ash, Save and Protect, Two Thousand Yards, and Deus Ex Machina quests explore just how far people are willing to go to avoid being left alone with their own fears.

Economic adjustments
Randomization of rewards for completing events
We previously announced that we would be updating the randomization system for the final rewards earned from completing events.
The current system is outdated and sometimes results in situations where you receive an unreasonably small reward for a complex event. After the update, you will always receive 100% of the base reward, and there’s a chance you’ll receive an increased reward.
Comparison of rewards
It is important to note that this comparison shows the minimum rewards that can be earned using the different randomization systems (the old and the new).
If you look at the long-term farm, you'll notice that the income you earn, if it has increased at all, has only increased slightly.
The main goal of the updated system is to address the issue of unfair rewards.
For example, when:

Other adjustments

Changed the sales limit for the Detector Components item at Arsen: 165 → 170.
Achievement Showcase
The right-hand column in the profile is changed and is now called Achievement Showcase. All settings for pinned statistics and achievements are now located in the profile customization section, in a new tab between the profile card and music.
Within Statistics and Achievements, the only features remaining are viewing and managing privacy settings for other players. The settings for the showcase itself are now flexible: you can customize each row individually and rearrange them in any order.
Added the ability to pin items in the Achievements Showcase. A line can contain 2 statistics, 1 achievement, or 3 items. You cannot change the number of elements within a row (for example, changing the number of elements from 3 to 2 or 4). You can only pin personal items. Items from your inventory and personal storage are added to the list if you are in a safe zone.
Interface and controls
• 
Player interactions menu: the menu that appears now does not block controls or capture the mouse cursor. You can still move and shoot. To select an action, use the hotkeys indicated on the buttons.
• 
Shop: when you left-click on an item in the Suitable for section on the style/motif page, the 3D model changes to show the selected item equipped with the style/motif. Minor issues with interactions involving item slots in sets are also fixed.
• 
Season Pass: a notification now appears when the level increases. Updated icons and tooltips for rewards.
• 
Task log: added the ability to pin exchange recipes.
• 
HUD: added highlighting for events required to complete active quests.
• 
Hideout: if another object is required to open an object, the tooltip now specifies which one.
• 
Weapon examination: now has its own button in the settings.
Map changes

The map now matches the current season's color palette.
•

Objects in the world are now displayed on the map as well.
Grace of Festivity
The new bundle is now available in the in-game store! It includes event currency, cases, seasonal crates, season levels, and Overdrives.
The first six purchases come with discounts of up to 75%. Now’s a good time to stock up!

Other changes and fixes
• 
Refined the quest chain at the start of the game.
• 
Changed sound design for Chernobyl Nuclear Power Plant: added ambient sounds and new music.
• 
Injectors are now unlocked as you progress through the tutorial and are available for purchase from merchants in all safe zones.
• 
Fixed an issue with sending private messages to players whose usernames contain a large number of consecutive underscores.
• 
Added sound effects when upgrading armor and weapons.
• 
Adjusted the position of the Bale bag on the back: it is now positioned slightly higher.
• 
Fixed kill tasks that required a specific weapon.
• 
Fixed a bug where a character could get stuck while climbing an obstacle, causing the character to slow down and damage to be incorrectly applied.
• 
Fixed game crashes with AMD drivers newer than version 26.8.1.
• 
Fixed a bug that prevented penalties to be added to spread in jumps in some cases.
• 
Fixed an issue where the appearance of items in the radial menu was not updated correctly when they were replaced or upgraded.
• 
Updated the model and animations of the RSh-12, as well as the textures of its motifs, and adjusted the visuals of cartridges in skins.
• 
The faction bonus to the selling price now also applies to the Fence in the Drunken Geiger Bar.
• 
Fixed the Twins being absent from the Signal dungeon.
• 
Fixed a game crash that occurred when opening the key holder during a trade with another player.
